newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy sees Hebron deal when he returns.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy sees Hebron deal when he returns.

text.p: U.S. envoy Dennis Ross said before leaving the Middle East on Wednesday that he expected Israel and the Palestinians to reach a Hebron deal after he returned to the region next week.

"I will be giving a positive report to President Clinton and I will be returning here no later than Monday particularly because the work is going very well and because I hope and expect that we will conclude an agreement shortly thereafter," Ross told reporters after meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the West Bank town of Ramallah.

Ross said members of his staff would stay behind to continue mediation efforts between Israelis and Palestinians to resolve final disputes blocking Israel's withdrawal from parts of Hebron in the West Bank.
"I am very pleased with the progress that has been made," he said.
Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met on Tuesday after months of deadlock in the talks on Hebron, where 400 Jewish settlers live among 100,000 Palestinians.
"We hope that we will have this agreement for the implementation of what had been agreed upon very soon," Arafat told reporters.
